items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: Well Ray Nance was a triple threat... he was just an all around musician's musician.

ctx.x: Well Ray Nance was a triple threat, or would you call him the quadruple threat. He was a good trumpet player, he had such terrific ideas, he was a terrific violinist, he could dance, he could sing, he was just an all around musician's musician. And they still listen to his chorus on the original rendition of "A Train." That's -- they still try to pattern it after that chorus. He played. He was too much, as we say, too much.

We've mentioned very few of the singers. We've talked a little bit about Ivy and we've mentioned Kay Davis but there were a long succession of singers. No one stayed very long, I guess Ivy stayed long, didn't she. How about some of those singers? Who do you think were the outstanding ones?
